business_problem: Decathlon's SQL-based review system and Elasticsearch synchronization model could not reliably handle hundreds to thousands of requests per second, global review traffic, and diverse content formats across more than 60 countries.
solution_summary: Decathlon rebuilt its global customer-review platform on MongoDB Atlas after a SQL plus Elasticsearch stack struggled with hundreds to thousands of requests per second and the complexity of synchronizing structured and unstructured review data across more than 60 countries. Atlas's document model lets the retailer store text, image, and video-heavy review records in a single system, while auto-scaling and sharding distribute traffic horizontally and keep data close to each region. The architecture uses primary nodes for writes, secondary nodes for reads, and a dedicated analytics node that aggregates across shards so global review queries do not slow local experiences. Zone-based sharding, automated rerouting, and quorum best practices give Decathlon a resilient review service that keeps operating even when individual nodes fail.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Stores and distributes global customer-review data while supporting sharding, failover, and analytics across regions.

data_flow: Customer reviews from more than 60 countries are written to MongoDB Atlas, where primaries handle writes, secondaries serve reads, and zone-based shards keep data close to local users. A dedicated analytics node aggregates data across shards so Decathlon can run global review queries without slowing regional experiences.
business_outcome: The Atlas-based platform now stays available through node failures, scales horizontally across 60-plus countries, and uses analytics nodes and sharding to keep local experiences fast while supporting global review analysis.
metrics: typically taking less than two seconds
architecture_clues: The legacy design tried to synchronize SQL and Elasticsearch for review data.
MongoDB Atlas uses primary nodes for writes and secondary nodes for reads.
A dedicated analytics node aggregates cross-shard data for global queries.
Odd-numbered nodes and strategic zone distribution are used for quorum and resilience.
evidence_quotes: Attempts to integrate Elasticsearch highlighted further challenges, particularly in managing the synchronization between SQL and Elasticsearch
MongoDB offered this, along with features like auto-scaling and shard capabilities to distribute load globally.
If a node fails, requests are automatically rerouted to another node, a process typically taking less than two seconds
With MongoDB, we've built a system where even during node failures, operations continue almost unnoticed.
